name: Customer Focus
definition: Leaders start with their customers and work backward. They work vigorously to earn and keep customer trust.

rows.situation: When a new piece of work is being scoped
rows.under: Starts with what is convenient to build, and hopes the customer will adapt.
rows.justRight: Starts with the customer need and works backward to the smallest thing that would serve it.
rows.over: Treats every customer request as a mandate and never ranks them.

rows.situation: When the customer has a reason to doubt you
rows.under: Hides the miss or delays the news until they ask.
rows.justRight: Tells them what happened, what you will do, and when. Then does that.
rows.over: Over-promises to restore the feeling of trust, and breaks it again.

rows.situation: When the product or the process has a defect the customer will feel
rows.under: Ships it and waits for the ticket.
rows.justRight: Fixes it before it reaches them when you can, and tells them when you cannot.
rows.over: Stops all other work for a cosmetic issue one customer mentioned once.

rows.situation: When the internal process and the customer need conflict
rows.under: Protects the process. The customer waits.
rows.justRight: Changes the process, or names the real constraint, so the customer is not paying for internal convenience.
rows.over: Breaks a sound process for one loud request and creates a worse experience for everyone else.

rows.situation: When you still have time to change the plan
rows.under: Asks the customer after the design is frozen.
rows.justRight: Gets a real signal from the people who will use it, then decides.
rows.over: Rewrites the plan with every comment and never ships.
